description:
Stochastic estimates of the permanental rank-deficiency rate at the small $k$ where the event is observable, checked against the values those cases are known to take, together with a measured cost profile for the predicate.

## Background

Direct estimation of permanental rank deficiency is confined to small $k$. At $k = 1$ the event is an all-zero column, with probability exactly $q^{-n}$ — about $169$ events per $10^{7}$ samples at $q = 3$, $n = 10$. At $k = 2$ the predicted rate is about $2q^{-n}$, similarly observable at moderate $n$. Beyond that the event probability falls as $k/q^{n}$ and no Monte Carlo campaign observes it.

These estimates are a pipeline check rather than a test of the cited theorem, whose hypothesis $k \le 0.1\sqrt{n}$ no observable $(n,k)$ satisfies, and they must say so. Their statistical treatment is the small-count regime: event counts are in the tens, where a normal-approximation interval is at its weakest, so exact intervals are used.

The predicate's cost profile is measured here rather than asserted. Its early exit is the reason testing the event needs no new kernel, and the claim that expected work per matrix is a small constant number of $k \times k$ permanents rather than $\binom{n}{k}$ of them is a measurement the repository requires to be receipted.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: An estimate of $\Pr[\mathrm{per\text{-}rank} < k]$ at $k = 1$ over at least three $(q, n)$ cells agrees with the exact $q^{-n}$, with agreement stated as an exact interval containing the exact value at a stated sample size and level.
- [hard] REQ-02: An estimate at $k = 2$ over at least two $(q, n)$ cells is reported with its exact interval beside the $\approx 2q^{-n}$ heuristic, and any disagreement is recorded rather than reconciled.
- [hard] REQ-03: Intervals are exact rather than normal-approximation, since event counts are in the tens.
- [hard] REQ-04: A committed receipt reports the measured mean number of $k \times k$ permanent evaluations per matrix at each measured $(q, n, k)$, confirming or contradicting that the early exit keeps expected work a small constant.
- [hard] REQ-05: The receipt records seeds, stream addresses, sample sizes, git revision, hardware and toolchain, so each estimate is regenerable.
- [hard] REQ-06: Draws come from a stream purpose distinct from every campaign cell's, so no validation draw can enter a published zero-fraction cell.
- [hard] REQ-07: The report of these estimates states that the measured $(n,k)$ lie outside the $k \le 0.1\sqrt{n}$ hypothesis, so agreement supports the implementation and the $k/q^{n}$ heuristic rather than the theorem in its proven range.

## Notes

An estimate that disagrees with its known value is a pipeline finding, not a mathematical one, and is recorded as such.
title: Observable-event rate estimates for permanental rank deficiency
